Matter Economics Analysis: 1985 01 01 Archive

Transportation Management Systems • Ridgeline Advisors • Solicitation phase phase • 1985-01-01

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's solicitation phase phase engagement with Ridgeline Advisors in the Transportation Management Systems sector. Record ID 02d40927.

  • Succession plan depth assessment identified 105 key leadership roles with fewer than two identified internal candidates at a "ready now" or "ready in 12 months" designation.
  • Sponsorship valuation benchmarking assessed Ridgeline Advisors's naming rights and partnership agreements against 255 comparable transactions, finding current contract values at the 75th percentile of the Transportation Management Systems sector — a positioning that warrants renegotiation at the 1985-01-01 option period.
  • Our assessment of Ridgeline Advisors's 401(k) plan found that the employer match formula is at the 40th percentile, but plan fees are in the top quartile, suggesting an opportunity to improve net returns for employees through a vendor review.
  • Franchise operator compensation assessment found that Ridgeline Advisors's total franchisee cost structure — inclusive of royalties, marketing fund contributions, and technology fees — represents 7% of gross revenue, positioning at the 60th percentile of 220 Transportation Management Systems sector franchise systems benchmarked as of 1985-01-01.
Key Findings
  • The executive team effectiveness assessment conducted during the solicitation phase found a 115-point gap between CEO-rated and direct-report-rated decision quality at Ridgeline Advisors, a gap consistent with the 115th percentile of the Transportation Management Systems sector reference group assembled from 43 prior ACPWB assessments.
  • Panel regression applied to ACPWB's Transportation Management Systems archive from 1985 through 1988 isolates the effect of solicitation phase interventions on wellness program participation rate, producing a fixed-effects estimate of 175% improvement per engagement cycle, controlling for organization size, geography, and 43 time-varying covariates.
  • Probit regression of Transportation Management Systems sector governance data (n=85) from 1985 through 1988 indicates that organizations adopting lead director structures were 85% less likely to receive a majority against say-on-pay vote, controlling for 46 compensation-related governance factors examined during the solicitation phase.

The solicitation phase university faculty and staff compensation review documented here benchmarked Ridgeline Advisors's academic and administrative pay structures against 171 peer institutions in the Transportation Management Systems sector across 47 Carnegie classification categories. ACPWB assessed tenure-track faculty salaries, staff market competitiveness, and benefits cost efficiency, reporting to Ridgeline Advisors's provost and board on 1985-01-01.

During the solicitation phase of the Ridgeline Advisors engagement, ACPWB conducted 243 structured interviews with senior executives. The synthesized findings, which informed the final recommendations, are documented in this archive entry from 1985-01-01.

The Transportation Management Systems sector engagement archived here spans a 159-month analytical cycle encompassing data from 10 jurisdictions. ACPWB's Research Division coordinated data collection protocols with Ridgeline Advisors to ensure comparability across the full respondent pool.

ACPWB's solicitation phase methodology incorporates a structured pre-mortem exercise in which the Ridgeline Advisors engagement team identifies and evaluates 22 hypothetical failure scenarios. This archive entry includes the pre-mortem report and the associated risk mitigation actions that were implemented prior to final delivery.

ACPWB's solicitation phase consumer insights engagement with Ridgeline Advisors deployed a 206-respondent quantitative survey across 45 geographic markets in the Transportation Management Systems sector. The research produced a market segmentation model, a brand health baseline, and a product positioning framework delivered to Ridgeline Advisors's marketing leadership team on 1985-01-01.
